signature.name: Detroit Institute of Arts
signature.detail: One of America's great art museums, home to Diego Rivera's monumental Detroit Industry murals and a world-class collection spanning centuries. It is the city's top must-see for first-time visitors. Tip: closed Mondays; book timed tickets online and allow at least two hours.

signature.name: Motown Museum
signature.detail: The original Hitsville U.S.A. house where the Motown sound was born, with studios and memorabilia that tell Detroit's music story. A pilgrimage for music fans. Tip: tours are guided and sell out, so reserve ahead; it is a short drive from downtown.

signature.name: The Henry Ford
signature.detail: A vast museum complex in Dearborn covering American innovation, with the Rosa Parks bus and presidential limousines, plus Greenfield Village next door. Plan a full day. Tip: buy a combined ticket online and arrive early to beat crowds.

signature.name: Belle Isle Park
signature.detail: A 982-acre island park in the Detroit River with a conservatory, aquarium, beach and skyline views. It is the city's green escape. Tip: drive or bike over; the park is free to enter and best on a sunny weekday.

signature.name: Detroit RiverWalk
signature.detail: A revitalized waterfront promenade along the Detroit River with views of Canada and public art. Ideal for a stroll or bike ride. Tip: go at sunset for the best skyline photos; it is free and open daily.

signature.name: Eastern Market
signature.detail: America's largest historic public market district, buzzing on Saturdays with local produce, food stalls and murals. A taste of Detroit life. Tip: come Saturday morning for the full market; bring cash for small vendors.

signature.name: Guardian Building
signature.detail: A 1929 Art Deco skyscraper with a stunning painted lobby often called a cathedral of commerce. Quick but memorable. Tip: the lobby is free to visit on weekdays during business hours; dress casually but respectfully.
